result.resourceBinding: the successful probe privately binds the exact loopback socket tuple, sole writable TMPDIR, and parent/child outside sentinels; the exact isolated CODEX_HOME is appended to the run result
result.writableSurface: the concrete Codex MVP rejects more than one writable root and requires that sole root to equal the closed TMPDIR environment value
result.processes: the bounded launcher kills the owned process group on every exit and records absent_after_exit only after ESRCH; a parent that abruptly exits 99 after spawning a child leaves no orphan
result.sockets: cleanup verifies each exact loopback TCP address is available, then closes the verification listener
result.paths: cleanup verifies the bound TMPDIR, CODEX_HOME, and randomized parent/child outside-sentinel paths are absent without deleting caller-selected paths
result.evidence: canonical evidence binds the run ID, exact socket tuple, ordered digests of run-owned paths, historical process-group result, and remaining-resource counts; raw local paths are absent
result.projection: only private clean, run-bound, resource-bound evidence can project cleanup: verified; zero, dirty, mutated-count, unbound, or cross-binding evidence cannot pass
result.tests: sandbox count-25, race, all-assurance, full CLI, vet, format, and Darwin/Linux/Windows compile-only checks passed
result.independentReview: approved the read-only verifier, exact resource binding, private pass provenance, abrupt-parent orphan proof, and truthful absent-after-exit semantics; no reviewer writes

limits: This task proves local Go subprocess, loopback, and filesystem behavior. It did not execute Codex, Seatbelt, a project command, the Mastra SDK, a receiver, a provider/model request, production coordinates, or an external control-plane operation.
Socket and path checks are bounded point-in-time observations, not atomic guarantees against later same-UID recreation.
Process-group absence is the launcher's bounded observation immediately after process exit; cleanup evidence does not claim a later process rescan.
The crash regression covers an abruptly exiting sandboxed parent and its orphan child. It does not claim recovery if the orchestrator itself dies.
Resource owners close sockets and remove run-owned paths before verification. The verifier performs no destructive deletion.
Maximum process-count enforcement remains a separate unresolved Phase 03 support/exit gate.
